This one is interesting, and I'm not sure what the right behavior here is.

The intention in the original PR is to have a display output like `symbol version (toolchain)`, e.g. `🦀 v.1.75.3 (stable)`. If we set this to `None` when the version is unknown, we get `🦀  (toolchain)` (with two intermediate spaces) as our output.

I think overall, I'd like to clean up a lot of these and figure out a sane naming/organization scheme. For instance, right now, the method `get_env_toolchain_override` sounds like it's retrieving an override from environmental variables, but really it's attempting to follow `rustup`'s procedure, which involves reading from the environment, checking toolchain and local override files, etc.

With the way things are currently organized and named, I find it difficult to think about what's necessary and what's not.

Somehow, there's a lifetime error that happens when you do that. I don't have the motivation to debug lifetime issues on chained methods at the moment, which is why I have this [weird set of assignments](https://github.com/starship/starship/pull/3414/files#diff-9916a3a9c5b9f49331e4569e3ef2d228d451eb39a98d44fcc37df570534b730fR233) in the current commit, but that's definitely something to tackle later.
